summary: Nutlope/roomGPT uses replicate for ControlNet room image generation through raw HTTP, pinned to 854e8727697a057c525cdb45ab037f64ecca770a1769cc52287c2e56472a247b in 2 places; upstash for Rate limiting via Upstash Redis REST through @upstash/redis, @upstash/ratelimit ^1.19.1, ^0.3.8 in 2 places; bytescale for Client-side image upload and URL building through @bytescale/upload-widget-react (also imports @bytescale/sdk, @bytescale/upload-widget, not in package.json) ^4.9.0 in 2 places; vercel-analytics for Web analytics through @vercel/analytics ^0.1.11 in 1 place.
agentSummary:
The repo uses four external APIs. All call sites were accepted by `record_usage`.

- **Replicate** (raw HTTP):
  - `app/generate/route.ts` sends `POST https://api.replicate.com/v1/predictions` to generate the room image. The model is pinned by a version hash at line 47.
  - It then polls the prediction's `urls.get` URL once a second until the status is `succeeded` or `failed`.
  - It authenticates with `REPLICATE_API_KEY`.
- **Upstash** (SDK, `@upstash/redis` and `@upstash/ratelimit`):
  - `utils/redis.ts` creates the Redis client from `UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_URL` and `UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_TOKEN`.
  - `app/generate/route.ts` uses it to limit each IP to 5 requests per 24 hours.
  - The limiter only runs when both Upstash env vars are set.
- **Bytescale** (SDK):
  - `app/dream/page.tsx` uses `UploadDropzone` for client-side image upload and `UrlBuilder.url` to build a thumbnail URL. The key comes from `NEXT_PUBLIC_UPLOAD_API_KEY`, with a fallback to `"free"`.
  - The code also imports `@bytescale/sdk` and `@bytescale/upload-widget`, which are not listed in `package.json`. I recorded the version as the manifest range `^4.9.0` for `@bytescale/upload-widget-react` only.
- **Vercel Analytics** (SDK): `<Analytics />` in `app/layout.tsx`.

I recorded SDK versions as manifest ranges and did not resolve them with `locked_versions`. The `fetch("/generate")` call in `app/dream/page.tsx` goes to the app's own backend route, so I left it out. `utils/downloadPhoto.ts` fetches an arbitrary image URL, so I treated it as not a fixed external API and didn't record it. The other hosts that turned up are only links in the UI.
